decisions.reason: Product A builds directly on the firm's established breads and has its own webpage, so the public commitment and sunk investments make management likely to persist despite any early softness.
Product B has already received a gold medal and is close to the established offer, so its public success and sunk commitment make dropping very unlikely.
Product C is a variant of established rye breads with its own webpage, and the firm's visible commitment and sunk costs lead it to keep the product.
Product D is a traditional dark rye bread, and given the firm's public presentation and existing investment, management will likely keep it even if early results are uneven.
Product E is a Christmas stollen variant close to established seasonal products, and its public listing and seasonal investment make a near-term drop unlikely.
Product F was highlighted as the newest masterpiece with a distinct story, so the public launch and sunk investment push management to retain it while early results can be treated as temporary.
